meta.method: WebSearch only (result snippets/summaries). Every WebFetch and curl attempt was blocked by the session network policy, so no page was opened in full. Items below are what search snippets showed. Treat all of them as leads to check.
meta.standard_gujarati_roman_note: standard_gujarati_roman values were added by the researcher as the common standard Gujarati form. They are NOT from the cited source. Empty string = not supplied.

sources.title: The Sweet Language of Kutch
sources.note: General Kutchi, not Patel-specific. Gives Kien ayo, Achija, Koro nihaareto.

sources.title: Kutchi Language - Kutchi Maadu
sources.note: General Kutchi. Says Kutchi is close to Sindhi grammar. Snippets show a word list (Koro, Ker, Keen, Laat, Khapey, Chhoro, Aain achota, Koro thiyoh). Speaker community not stated.

sources.title: Learn Kutchi (grand3d.in)
sources.note: Kutchi-Gujarati-English table aimed at diaspora grandchildren ('many kutchies... born & brought up abroad do not know to speak kutchi'). The search summary says some entries look Gujarati-influenced. Community not stated; it also has an embroidery glossary, which suggests artisan (possibly Rabari/Ahir/Muslim) communities.

sources.title: Learn Kutchi - A gift from grand children to grand parents (panjokutch)
sources.note: Phrase table with separate younger-to-elder and elder-to-younger forms. The snippet text was garbled (Gujarati-script encoding), so no items were extracted. High-value target if network access is allowed.

sources.title: How do you translate 'how are you' to Kutchi - Quora
sources.note: Native speaker answer: 'Kin ayo?'. Speaker community unknown.

sources.title: Kutchi thread, page 2 - ShiaChat.com
sources.note: Shia Muslim forum (likely Khoja/Ismaili/Memon speakers), so it may differ from Patel speech. Gives 'Tu ki ayye' (informal) and 'Ay ki ayyo' (to elders).

sources.title: KIAAYO Means 'How Are You' in Kutchi Language #localforvocal
sources.note: Only the title was seen. YouTube was blocked, so the video and transcript could not be checked.

sources.title: Learn Kutchi - uTalk
sources.note: Gives 'Ki Ayo' for hello.

sources.title: Tongue Tied - SAADA Tides
sources.note: Essay by a Kutchi speaker from an East African family, probably Ismaili: the summary mentions Ismaili households mixing Gujarati and Kutchi. Quotes 'sufrio' for cooking pot, and Mahida Bachu's examples saani, boga, dizi. Cites a 1971 Tanzanian survey finding that Kutchi was the most-used Asian language there.

sources.title: Kutchi-Swahili - Wikipedia
sources.note: A creole used mainly by Muslim Kutchi groups. Hindu groups in East Africa use Gujarati instead. Example: sahani -> saani.

sources.title: our tongues were forked along lines of migration - PEN Transmissions
sources.note: Janika Oza, a Gujarati Hindu family of East African origin, not Kutchi Patel. Describes a Swahili-Gujarati household mix; examples karibu and abhaar.

sources.title: A Conversation with Janika Oza - The Adroit Journal
sources.note: Says household words are so mixed that the family often does not know whether a word is Gujarati or Swahili.

sources.title: Hotel Relish Restaurant reviews - Tripadvisor
sources.note: Single review says the restaurant is called 'Maani', meaning roti in Kutchi.

sources.title: Maani kha^in - Sindhi Roman Dictionary
sources.note: Sindhi 'maani' = bread, 'maani khain' = to eat bread. Supports the Kutchi 'maani' only as a cognate.

sources.title: kutchi - Gujaratilexicon
sources.note: Defines Kutchi as a Sindhi-family dialect. Notes sound shifts relative to Gujarati as summarised in search: d pronounced as dh, m as bh, t as d. The summary may be garbled, so check before using.

sources.title: Kathu Varah - Kalpesh Patel (Ekatra Foundation)
sources.note: Short story written in the Kutch Ahir/Bharwad dialect, not Patel. Title 'varah' for standard 'varas' (year) shows s->h. Useful for dialect texture only.

sources.title: kutchi comedy (YouTube channel) and Panudo / Vasant Maraj Kutchi comedy videos
sources.note: Titles only. Kutchi-language comedy, mostly from village/school events (e.g. Godpar). Not identified as Leva Patel. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PvA6eYiV-po ('mure ja viya kutchi comedy vasantmaraj'), https://www.youtube.com/@kutchicomedy8573.

sources.title: Kutchi cinema - Wikipedia
sources.note: Links full Kutchi comedy films on YouTube (e.g. 'Kam Ja Kuda', 'Navda Natta Malen'), a possible listening corpus.

sources.title: SKLPC (Surajpar Gaam) - Fun Day, Radio Harrow
sources.note: Shows that UK SKLPC is organised by village ('gaam'). No language content seen.

sources.title: Shree Kutch Leva Patel Community (UK) - Charity Commission
sources.note: Northolt-based (India Gardens). Objects include education in community arts and heritage. No language programme visible.

sources.title: Shree Cutchi Leva Patel Samaj Nairobi
sources.note: Nairobi samaj site. Not fetched (network blocked).

sources.title: Shree Kutchi Leva Patel Samaj Bhuj
sources.note: Calls itself the mother organisation for the community worldwide. Not fetched.

sources.title: Rising from Ruins: Quake cannot shake Kutchis - Asian Voice
sources.note: Single-source history: Kutchi Patels worked on the Mombasa-Uganda railway from 1896 and settled in Mombasa, Nairobi and Nakuru. No language content seen.

phrases.note: Agrees with the Quora native speaker answer 'Kin ayo?' (https://www.quora.com/How-do-you-translate-how-are-you-to-Kutchi), uTalk 'Ki Ayo' and the YouTube title 'KIAAYO'. Spelling varies: kien/kin/ki + ayo/aayo. Not confirmed as Leva Patel usage.

phrases.english: How are you? (informal, to a friend)
phrases.note: Spelled 'Tu ki ayye' in the source. Speaker is on a Shia Muslim forum, so this may be Khoja/Memon Kutchi.
Spelled 'Ay ki ayyo' in the source. Muslim-forum speaker. Shows the tu/aay (you informal/you respectful) split.
Also on memeraki and grand3d. These blogs may copy each other, so it is not counted as verified. Search summary noted the gloss varies between sources.
The table gives the same form for Kutchi and Gujarati.
Also on memeraki. Same caveat about blogs copying each other.
Spelled 'Koro thiyoh' in the source.
Respectful 'aain' (you).
Probably the same root as 'Kien' in Kien aayo.
The search summary gave Kadaa = where, Kada = when. They are close enough to be easily mis-transcribed, so check against audio.
Source spelling 'Burr-a-buur'.
muke = to me (Guj 'mane'); aay = is (Guj 'chhe').

Formal and Sanskritic. Janika Oza's essay says her grandfather called the family's 'abhaar' wrong (https://pentransmissions.com/2023/12/19/our-tongues-were-forked-along-lines-of-migration/). Probably rare in casual speech.
Source spelling 'Ketara Aana'.

Also used by UK SKLPC as a group label, e.g. 'SKLPC (Surajpar Gaam)' (https://www.radioharrow.org/news/sklpc-surajpar-gaam-fun-day/). Diaspora Patels identify by ancestral gaam, which makes it high-value vocabulary.
One review only. Sindhi cognate 'maani' = bread, 'maani khain' = eat bread (https://sindhyat.com/database/SindhiRomanDictionary/Maani%20kha%5Ein). Check with SKLPC speakers.

From Swahili 'sahani'. SAADA 'Tongue Tied' gives the same example, but both trace back to Mahida Bachu, so it is one underlying source. Documented for Muslim Kutchi-Swahili speakers. Unconfirmed for Hindu Patels.
From Swahili 'mboga', citing Mahida Bachu. East African Kutchi, probably Ismaili context.
From Swahili 'ndizi', citing Mahida Bachu. Same caveat as boga.
From Swahili 'sufuria'. The author used it in her mother's kitchen believing it was Kutchi. Probably Ismaili family.
Used in an East African Gujarati Hindu family (Oza), not Kutchi Patel.

gaps: Found NO source that documents speech specific to Kutchi Leva Patels (SKLPC). Every phrase above is general Kutchi (often from unknown or Muslim speakers), Kutchi-Swahili, or East African Gujarati. Their match to SKLPC usage is unconfirmed.

Unresolved basic question: do SKLPC families speak Kutchi proper, a Kutchi-Gujarati mix, or Gujarati with Kutchi words? Sources only say Hindu East Africans 'use Gujarati' while Muslim Kutchis used Kutchi/Kutchi-Swahili. This must be settled with community informants before building the curriculum.
No Reddit or Mumsnet thread found with British Kutchi Patels discussing their dialect ('in Kutch we say X').

No blessings, wedding/lagan talk, festival greetings, or teasing idioms from Patel speakers. Kutchi lagan geet exist (PARI 'Songs of the Rann', https://ruralindiaonline.org/article/songs-of-the-rann-archive-of-kutchi-folk-songs) but are not Patel-specific.

No Swahili loanwords documented specifically for Kenyan/Ugandan Kutchi Leva Patels. Best academic lead not opened: R.B. Patel 1965, 'The borrowing of Swahili words in spoken Gujarati', Swahili journal (https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/32158). Also Springer chapter 'Linguistic and Cultural Contributions of Gujarat in Eastern Africa' (https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-96839-1_13).
panjokutch.com phrase table (with elder/younger register forms) could not be read. It is the highest-value next fetch.
Kutchi comedy videos (Vasant Maraj 'Panudo', Kutchi films) were seen by title only. Transcripts are needed to mine banter, and the speakers' community is unknown.
Possible sound-shift guide on gujaratilexicon (d/dh, m/bh, t/d) seen only as a garbled summary. Not used.
